reviews.text: 在今年，我关注到了一款非常有趣的“科幻题材”游戏《KingMakers》，在游戏的PV中，我们看到的是在中世纪的背景下，玩家扮演一名身穿中世纪盔甲的“骑士”，身骑摩托车，手持AK与那些手持剑盾弓箭的中世纪敌人战斗，非常无厘头，甚至可以开坦克去轰炸城堡，有点神金。而且我等待这款游戏发售的过程中，我关注到了本作《Knight Within》似乎使用了同样的背景，同样的无厘头风格，只是制作的更加简陋，但是抢占了游戏的先机，提前发售了本作游戏。 本作主打的同样是在中世纪的城堡时代背景下，让玩家手持现代自动远程武器进行各种任务，击败各种敌人。然而本作中的敌人似乎都是幽灵敌人，在较为模糊的画质下，击败这些幽灵敌人后敌人会灰飞烟灭，并且敌人也是无限生成的，玩家不需要过多关注敌人，而是要把注意力放在任务的完成上。游戏的关卡是随机选择的，每个观察出现的任务也是随机的，玩家来到任务点会告知玩家任务的目标，有的是要求杀敌数，有的是护卫任务，也有其他的各种各样的任务类型，任务种类倒是挺丰富的，但是敌人的种类却比较淡薄，只有几种，针对不同的敌人玩家需要使用不同的方式去应对，例如有的敌人需要寻找它隐藏在重甲下的弱点，才容易击破。游戏中玩家的枪械子弹是有限制的，但是是可以通过击败一些敌人掉落（微乎其微），也可以通过完成任务，在任务点附近出现，也可以使用空投技能支援弹药。游戏的体验过程中，我感觉弹药还是比较缺乏的，尤其是面对成群的敌人时，倾泻弹药会消耗非常快。当玩家没有了远程武器后，可以使用近战武器，例如刀剑等对敌人进行攻击，但是很明显，游戏的打击感比较差，似乎游戏就是希望玩家能够使用枪械对抗这些幽灵骑士，并不那么推荐近战武器。 游戏主打的是联机模式，本作支持最多4人联机，并且支持匹配系统，但是在我游玩的几局中，我并没有匹配过任何人，同时在线的玩家不高于10人，这就是这种联机游戏比较尴尬的地方。玩单人游玩确实存在一定的难度，当通关关卡后，大家可以在自己的城堡中进行一些外观和武器的买卖，这套系统并不陌生了，末世鼠疫，暗潮等作品中均是采用类似的模式，本作应该也是模仿的这类游戏做出的系统。 很多的优势在于当玩家激起了对这类题材的兴趣后，抢先发售了游戏，让许多对这个题材感兴趣的玩家，首先尝试了一把，赢在了速度上，但是整体游戏还需要打磨，目前感觉游戏性还差了很多，想要真的想在游戏市场中占据一定的份额，需要大刀阔斧的改一下。 [code] 点击关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/26214428] 電玩狂熱愛好者 [/url] ，以获取更多游戏评测、资讯、攻略 [/code]

The creator of [i]Knights Within[/i] seems to have wondered "what if medieval knights had modern firearms?" and decided to made a game to answer just that question. The game consists of missions where one or more players traverse a map looking for objectives; each completed objective gives the player a choice of a power up, like a classic roguelike game. Players can also customise their characters in three ways: [list] [*]changing the equipped weapons: melee, firearm and a "spell" that must be charged during missions, as well as modifiers for each of them (e.g. a shield mod that stuns nearby enemies after blocking enough hits, or a gun mod that increases magazine size); [*]picking a class that favours a certain play style, like dodging through enemies or being more effective at stunning; [*]equipping passive traits from up to three skill trees that enhance some of the player's actions, depending on whether they want to be more effective at shooting, or blocking, or killing bosses, and so on. [/list] There is also cosmetic customisation: it's not very in-depth but it's certainly a welcome sight, especially on multiplayer missions where one may want to look different from their teammates. Missions in general have a lot going on, from random storms to enemy hordes to hidden locations where players can unlock new skill trees. It's also possible to find gadgets that give special abilities while on a mission, like an energy shield that blocks projectiles, and up to three can be equipped at a time. Even better, the developer is constantly at work on game updates, to the point where I'm not sure how long the content of this review will stay relevant. I wish every early access game received updates this often! So far, the only flaw I've found with this game consists of the enemies: the player is constantly chased by wraiths with assorted medieval weapons (both melee and ranged), as well as "elite" wraiths that specialise in certain attacks ([i]brutes[/i] will interrupt you and throw you to the ground, [i]enforcers[/i] will hit you with a slowing beam and so on) but there are so many of them that they can't help but feel generic and samey after a while. Bosses tend to have the same problem: they have unique names and movesets but they eventually all boil down to [list] [*]2 or 3 melee swings [*]linear or circular area-of-effect the player has to dodge [*]energy bubble that negates the player's bullets [/list] and fighting them is not very exciting. With some luck, we will eventually get new enemies that better stand out! This, however, is my real only issue with the game, and it hasn't prevented me from enjoying Knights Within for over 50 hours. It's definitely a thumbs up from me.

This game is very difficult to like. While I understand that this is a solo endeavour, my gripes with the game isn't with the obvious bought assets, the poor sound and music design, the repetitive game-play. I understand that the developer is aiming for a 3rd person vampire survivor, the game falls short in ways that are quite egregious if not outright malicious. In it's current state, asking for 15 USD is really hard to swallow [b]Running between objectives[/b] The 2 maps that were available to me were barren. Sometimes there's a 2 minute trek between objects of nothing but just walking around and killing the same enemies. I understand the need to at least have SOMETHING to do between mob killing, but having "objectives" where you need to stick around a point is more tedious than fun. If the goal is to mix up the gamplay loop, making the player run around a mostly empty map is fun for about 5 minutes. Risk of rain at least had interesting landscape to look at and vertical movement. There's a jump option but nothing to traverse. I cannot think of another reason why this needs to be in your game at the current state beyond trying to pad out game time. [b]Questing and Leveling[/b] While it's nice to see that there will be classes some time down the road, I'm not sure anyone would bother playing the game enough to unlock it. in my 3 hours of play time, I've managed to finish the first difficulty once and got close to finishing the second difficulty. My character is level 10 at time of review and I have yet to unlock every customisation slot. If there's class progression some time down the line my suggestion would be to lower the barrier of entry while your game is in beta so people can at least experience it. Again, this design decision seems to be built around retention and not gameplay, dangling more content beyond the steam refund window is a possible motive. Once again, I understand that this is a solo project. As a developer you need to understand that anyone paying for the current experience is basically doing it to support you IN SPITE of the current state of the game. The least you can do is respect their time a little and not let them walk away feeling like they've been cheated.

[This product was received for free] My first few hours in the game were pretty fun and interesting! It took a moment to figure out how to use all my attacking and movement options to my advantage, and it's nearly satisfying to swing a sword and a gun around. If you want to stay ahead of the enemies mutation curve, completing the objectives faster is the way to go. Though this isn't my first time playing a roguelite, this is the first objective-based roguelite I've played and so far, it's a BLAST. I'm impressed by the quality of the gameplay at early access release, and judging by the pre-existing reviews and dev notes, I know this will grow into an amazing game. If you like Helldivers, Risk of Rain, and a little souls-like combat this is another game for you! Wants for future updates: -I would appreciate there being signs or details in the hub world that tell the player where the armour upgrades are, as well as the balcony and prestige upgrades. -Brighter environments/textures: often I would miss a few enemies, or the boss because everything around me is dark, especially in the forest areas. -Louder & Visible Parry (I think its a little difficult to hear above everything else, even after adjusting my audio sliders -Audio Sliders save after closing window -Proper tutorial run: Instead of having tutorial boxes pop up and lock your camera in your first real run (distracting, costs time and health), the tutorial should be a mini run covering the types of interactables, objectives, and enemies in the world and how to move around effectively. -Dynamic Music & More Music: Sometimes I'd find myself fighting for an objective or boss in utter silence. Sometimes, I'd be fighting the Fallen to unfitting music. WE WILL ENDURE
